Where I got to, and why I'm stopping here rather than shipping a half-built archive
I read the whole tree out of dump.txt (317 files, byte-verified against the dump's own SHA/size metadata — no truncation), and I started building M6 Slice 10. I did not finish the archive, so there is nothing to extract yet. Here is the state, in the order you'll care about.

1. On "some tests are now failing" — I cannot see the failure, and I want to say so plainly
claude-terminal.txt in the project is stale: every run in it predates Slice 9. It shows SecondGuest_JoinsAndSeesOrderLiveWithRosterUpdate [SKIP], dotnet test at 971/0 failed, and MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 at 8 passed / 7 skipped. Meanwhile dump.txt (generated 2026-08-03 17:55) does contain Slice 9's scenario 5. So the only test output I have is from before the code I'd be diagnosing.

I read scenario 5 line by line against TableOrderSurface.razor and could not find a defect: every selector matches the markup (ul.table-roster > li, span.table-roster-name, the you chip, li.order-party-order, div.order-line-main, span.order-party-line-name, the chip-ok/chip-warn badges), RosterName/BillName both fall back to display name, and ReadOpenSittingAsync orders by joined_at.

If it is still red, please paste the failing output — one scenario name and its message is enough. Guessing at it would waste a slice.

2. One real latent defect I did find, and fixed
TableOrderJourneys.SendAsync waited for #table-order-surface p.status-success. That element survives from the previous send, so any scenario that sends twice can have the wait satisfied by the old confirmation before the new send has committed. Scenario 5 only escapes this by accident (StageItem nulls _sendStatus, and StageAsync waits for the render that does it). It also meant a refused send could only ever surface as a 30-second timeout.

I've rewritten it to judge a send by state rather than copy: §11.1 clears the basket only on an accepted event, so the poll watches for the basket emptying or ul.order-reject-list appearing, and either ends the wait immediately. That's also the mechanism Slice 10 needs, since scenario 7 is about a refusal.

3. A documentation defect worth your eyes
docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md contains M5 Slice 3 twice — identical ### headings at lines 1550 and 2506. The copy at 1550 is the accident (it sits between M5 Slice 2 and M4 Slice 2). Since you don't want scripts, I was going to ship the whole corrected 4,758-line file inside the archive rather than as a cat >> you'd have to run. I verified it extracts byte-exact from the dump (329,063 bytes, matching the dump's own metadata), so regenerating it is safe.

I also checked all fifteen docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-*.md files: every one is already merged into BUILD_PROGRESS.md. So the deletion list would have been those fifteen plus docs/_append/M6-SLICE-9-CHANGES.md (a stray copy of the old root _CHANGES.md).

4. What Slice 10 was going to be, and the design problem I hit
§16.3 scenario 7 is "Guest tries to remove the fulfilled line → whole batch rejected with per-op reason; removing their pending line succeeds."

The product will not let a guest reach that server rule from a seat. NarratedOrderLine.GuestMayRemove is false for a fulfilled line, so §11.1 renders no tick box on one; and OrderStaging.PruneRemovals unticks any mark that goes stale, on every LoadAsync. So the literal path exists only as a millisecond-wide race, which is not a test I'd write.

The honest version is three acts, all deterministic:

(a) "Tries to remove the fulfilled line." The guest ticks their pending soup; the kitchen fulfills it; §9's LineFulfillmentChanged reaches the guest's circuit, the tick is dropped, the box disappears, and §11.1 writes the unticking notice. The surface refusing is the answer.
(b) "Whole batch rejected with per-op reason." Reached the one way a guest still can — §7's documented path: stage an item, the kitchen 86s it, Send. The batch also carries a good removal of the pending pie, and asserting that the pie survives is what makes it all-or-nothing rather than partial.
(c) "Removing their pending line succeeds." Take the 86'd item out, Send the removal alone.
Product changes needed: one — a order-prune-notice class on the prune notice <p>, because three other p.status-error elements live inside that island and there was no way to address this one. Same reasoning as Slice 9's .order-party-line-name; no CSS rule behind it, nothing changes on screen.

5. Files that were going to change
Path	Change
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Table/TableOrderSurface.razor	one added class (done)
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/TableOrderJourneys.cs	removal/unstage/refusal journeys + the SendAsync fix (done)
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/KitchenJourneys.cs	EightySixAsync (not written)
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/EndToEndScenarios.cs	scenario 7 (not written)
docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md	dedupe + Slice 10 block (not written)
_CHANGES.md	(not written)
Two of six are done and sitting in the sandbox, which does not survive. Say continue and I'll rebuild them and ship the complete .tar.gz with the deletion list — and if you have the failing output by then, send it and I'll take that first.

One thing worth flagging while it's fresh: I caught four CS4007 errors in my own new code (an await inside an interpolated string that binds to DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler — a ref struct) and hoisted them out. That trap is already documented in TableJourneys.cs; it bites every time.

Claude reached its tool-use limit for this turn.

I verified each of the seventeen BUILD_PROGRESS-*.md files by exact substring against the docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md in this archive first — all seventeen are already merged, so nothing is lost. The eighteenth, M6-SLICE-9-CHANGES.md, is a stray copy of last slice's delivery note; Slice 9's ledger row stays in BUILD_PROGRESS.md. The full list is in _CHANGES.md if you'd rather delete them one by one.

docs/_append/ is retired. This archive ships the whole of docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md, so there is no cat >> to run — and that also fixes the duplicated M5 Slice 3 section Slice 9 flagged (4,758 → 4,701 lines).

What the scenario found
§16.3 asks for "guest tries to remove the fulfilled line → whole batch rejected." That cannot happen through the surface. GuestMayRemove is false for a fulfilled line, §11.1 renders the tick box only where it holds, and PruneRemovals drops stale marks. The only route left is a millisecond race against an in-process broadcaster. So the scenario asserts what the product actually does — the surface refusing on the guest's behalf, then §6.5.9's all-or-nothing reached the one way a guest still can (§7's "stage it, then it goes unavailable" path), then the same tick committing once the batch is clean.

Writing it turned up three defects:

The unticking notice nobody ever saw. One commit raises two notifications — IOrderWorkflow publishes OrderLinesChanged then LineFulfillmentChanged — and this surface subscribes to both. LoadAsync opened with _pruneNotice = null;, so the first pass wrote the sentence and the second erased it microseconds later. In practice a guest's tick vanished with no explanation.
Unstage left the previous refusal on screen. StageItem and ToggleRemoval clear _rejection; Unstage did not — so the edit most likely to resolve a refusal was the one that left it up.
Waits a previous action could satisfy. SendAsync and FulfillLineAsync both waited on status sentences that survive on screen. Scenario 5 escapes only by accident. Both now wait on state: basket-empties vs. reject-panel for a send, line-leaves-the-pass for a fulfillment.
On the failing tests
Still no output to work from — claude-terminal.txt predates Slice 9 and shows everything green. Defect 3 is the one candidate I found by inspection, and it's fixed. If something is still red, paste the message; these failures are written to be the diagnosis.

Expected
Command	Expect
dotnet test	971 total, 0 failed, 15 skipped — unchanged
bash scripts/ci_local.sh --with-all	green
MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 dotnet test tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests	15 total, 10 passed, 5 skipped
10/5 is arithmetic, not observation — it assumes scenario 5 went green. Nothing here touches scenario 5's assertions.

One thing to watch: FulfillLineAsync changed behaviour and scenario 6 uses it too. If scenario 6 regresses, that's the first place to look. _CHANGES.md has a failure-message table for the rest.

Next is scenario 8 — exactly one reminder — which wants KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS threaded through the harness the way the rotation window already is.
